characters.name: Simon Blackquill
characters.description1: A prosecutor who excels at psychological manipulation. As far as psychology goes, he's kind of like my senior, I guess.

characters.name: Taifu Toneido
characters.description1: A rakugo storyteller of fifty-five years who is famous for his soba-based routines. He has two disciples under him in his troupe.

characters.name: Bucky Whet
characters.description1: My client for this case, and the fourth head of Whet Soba. He's still got a lot to learn about noodle making.

characters.name: Nahyuta Sahdmadhi
characters.description1: A prosecutor from the Kingdom of Khura'in. He's also known as the "Last Rites Prosecutor."

characters.name: Geiru Toneido
characters.description1: Balloon artist and her master's senior disciple. She has twelve years of performance under her belt.

characters.name: Uendo Toneido
characters.description1: A rakugo storyteller and junior disciple after Geiru. He has less experience than Geiru, yet he's become higher ranked than her.

evidences.name: Attorney's Badge
evidences.description1: My attorney's badge. It's lost that "brand-new" shine, but that just shows how far I've come.

evidences.name: Backstage Diagram
evidences.description1: Diagram of the backstage area showing the location of the stage, the dressing room, and the yard. [caption] The door to the dressing room and the door to the yard face one another. When the door of the yard is open, the door blocks the view from the yard to the dressing room.

evidences.name: Crime Scene Report
evidences.description1: The crime scene took place in the theater dressing room. Master Toneido was found with his face thrust into a large soba bowl.
evidences.description2: Contains photos of the crime scene. The victim's dying message is clearly visible in them. Includes additional info.

evidences.name: Taifu's Autopsy Report
evidences.description1: The time of death is between 2 PM and 5 PM. The cause of death is suffocation. It reads: Time of death: May 12, 2 PM - 5 PM; Cause of death: Suffocation. Nothing was found in his lungs.

evidences.name: Whet Soba Deed
evidences.description1: Found in the victim's possession. It's the deed to the soba shop. The deed holder is Bucky Whet.

evidences.name: Invitation
evidences.description1: The invitation Simon received from Master Toneido to the show commemorating Uendo's name succession and promotion. It states that the show "Time Soba" was to be performed by Master Toneido himself.

evidences.name: Simon's Statement
evidences.description1: Simon's eyewitness account of the time of the incident.
evidences.description2: Simon's eyewitness account of the time of the incident. Includes additional info.

evidences.name: Karuta Cards
evidences.description1: Karuta cards in the victim's dressing room. They spell out "WHET NO 4."
evidences.description2: Karuta cards in the victim's dressing room. They originally spelt out "OWEN 4TH" as shown.

evidences.name: Taifu's Note
evidences.description1: A note thought to have been written by the victim before his death.

testimonies.testimony: From 4 PM to a little after 4:20 PM, when Shisho's body was found...
...Simon and I were standing in the hallway in front of the dressing room.
Before Uendo discovered the body, the only person who had gone in there was Bucky.
Come to think of it, a little while before Bucky showed up, Jugemu was barking like mad!
I was in the yard, but the door was wide open, so I could keep watch on the dressing room.

source.evidence_span: The door to the dressing room and the door to the yard face one another. When the door of the yard is open, the door blocks the view from the yard to the dressing room.
source.testimony_span: I was in the yard, but the door was wide open, so I could keep watch on the dressing room.
source.explanation: If the door to the yard was wide open, it would've blocked the view from the yard, making it impossible to see the dressing room.

turns.summarizedContext: The witness Geiru describes who he saw before the crime.
reasoning: Fact 1: The witness claims she saw the dressing room from the yard while the door was wide open.
Fact 2: The evidence suggests that the open door to the yard would block the view of the dressing room.
Prop 1: If the view is blocked, one cannot see into the blocked location.
